text:
alex: FYI saw a ~3x spike in OOM rate on g5-pool-2 around 21:10 UTC after yesterday's kernel selection tweak. stack traces attached in logs but high-level looks like KV prefix cache + workspace fragmentation.

lina: ugh. which kernel change? was it the attention kernel fallback to fp16-merge?

alex: yes, we switched kernel selector to prefer merged-attn when seq_len>1024. the perf was OK but memory patterns shifted.

sam: can you paste the OOM trace? small snippets are fine.

alex: logs (short):
```
OOM at 0x7f12: alloc 256MB failed
caller: workspace_pool::reserve(size=52428800)
kv_cache::evict_candidate -> returned none
```

lina: looks like workspace pool tried to reserve for batching + kernel workspace and failed because kv eviction couldn't free contiguous slabs.

maya: also seeing a drop in prefix cache hit-rate right before the OOMs. hit-rate from 0.78 -> 0.46 over 5m on hot shards.

ryan: can we get sequence length distribution during the spike? might be more long-context requests that force larger workspace.

alex: querying metrics now: `sum by (seq) (requests{pool=g5-pool-2}[$__rate_interval])` -> ~12% of requests had seq_len >= 2048 in that window.

sam: interesting. so combined effects: longer sequences -> different kernel chosen -> larger kernel workspace + kv cache pressure -> fragmentation -> OOM.

lina: two parallel levers to try: 1) reduce contiguous workspace demand by forcing per-kernel workspace caps / enable small-chunk allocator reuse; 2) reduce KV cache footprint temporarily by setting shard TTL down or fast-evict cold prefixes.

alex: quick experiment suggestion: set `workspace_max_contiguous=48MB` and enable `slab_reuse=true` on canary nodes to see if fragmentation decreases. also add a short-term policy: `kv.prefixcache.snooze_ttl=30s` for cold shards to free early.

maya: I ran a local sim of shard hit-rate vs TTL: lowering TTL from 5m -> 30s reduces memory by ~40% but hit-rate drops from 0.78 -> 0.60; however effective latency impact in pipeline is small because most misses are cheap due to prefix prefetch.

ryan: ok, but we should avoid regressing end-to-end latency. can we do a canary rollout with metric gates: OOMs, p99 latency, token cost, and prefix miss tail?

sam: yes. propose canary group: 5 instances in us-west, enable workspace cap + slab_reuse, set `kv.snooze_ttl` to 30s for shards with load < 0.1 RPS, keep other shards unchanged. Gate: no OOMs for 30m, p99 latency <= baseline+5%.

lina: one more idea: tweak kernel-selector heuristic to prefer smaller-workspace kernel if expected batching depth > 4. We have a cheap estimator: if batch_size_estimate > 4 && seq_len>1024 -> prefer split-attn variant.

alex: added that to the canary config as a soft override.

devops-bot: deploy triggered: canary/kv-oom-mitigation -> 5 nodes in pool g5-pool-2. change-set: workspace_max_contiguous=48MB; slab_reuse=true; kv.snooze_ttl=30s for low-load shards; kernel_selector.soft_override=split-attn-on-high-batch.

maya: monitoring dashboards updated: new panels for contiguous_free_frag_pct, kv_snooze_evictions, kernel_workspace_bytes_by_kernel.

ryan: action items: (1) Observe canary for 1h, collect p99, OOM count, & prefix miss tail. (2) If stable, roll to 20% traffic and run perf eval suite. (3) Postmortem plan if OOMs persist: capture heapmap + workspace allocation traces and revert kernel selector change.

alex: I'll own the canary and run the perf eval. tagging @lina and @maya for followup on simulation and TTL tuning. :thumbsup:

lina: I'll run the hit-rate vs user-impact sim with synthetic workload (hot-cold mix) and share numbers in #eng-runtime later today.

sam: if canary shows improvement we should also consider longer-term: compacting allocator, per-shard soft caps, and improving reclaim API to support async eviction when allocator fails.

ryan: agreed. also add a metric alarm: contiguous_free_frag_pct < 12% -> page us oncall. we almost missed this.

alex: noted. will set alarm. closing thread for now until canary reports.
